summary: Bearish skew unchanged. Updated Reuters oil report shows Brent $96.14 and WTI $84.88, broadly consistent with the prior elevated range. Overseas relief persists; no fresh US cash confirmation.
bullish: QQQ recovered 3.73 percentage points from morning observation.
Russell 2000 and Dow closed higher; reported 10Y yield fell.
Equal-weight RSP gained 0.78% while SPY fell 0.30% in a secondary closing report.
FT and WSJ report Asian technology-heavy markets rebounding Thursday; proposed tariffs may replace existing levies rather than stack.
IBD reports Nasdaq-100 futures +1.05% versus S&P futures +0.7% overnight; exact quote time unavailable.
IBD reports both NQ and ES futures up 0.55%; holiday relief persists.
FT reports ASML +2.5% and Stoxx 600 +1.5% Thursday, indicating overseas technology relief.
Reuters reports both Nasdaq and S&P futures approximately +0.7%; Barron's reports +0.7% and +0.8% respectively, exact quote times unavailable.
bearish: QQQ lagged SPY by 0.36 percentage points at close.
Reuters reports semiconductor and AI credit stress; VIX rose despite recovery.
SMH reportedly lost 8% over five sessions; secondary SOX report indicates severe weakness, exact timestamp unavailable.
Oil supply disruption risk is corroborated by Reuters; inflation sensitivity remains elevated.
Curated core PCE 3.3% versus 3.2% consensus and GDP 4.3% versus 3.6% forecast reinforce tightening risk; tariff proposals are not yet effective.
S&P CreditWatch Negative on Nvidia AA rating adds financing/governance risk; no downgrade or isolated price reaction confirmed.
IBD reports Micron down 4.5% Wednesday; latest reported NQ futures no longer outperform ES.
Reuters reports China reserves the right to respond to tariffs; Korean chipmakers pared early gains according to FT.
Reuters reports Brent $96.25 and WTI $84.78 after renewed reported Middle East supply disruptions; WSJ independently corroborates rising oil. Exact quote times unavailable.

editorial.marketOverview: US cash markets are closed for Thanksgiving. Reuters reports overseas equities recovering as tariff details appear less severe than feared, while crude remains elevated. Wednesday semiconductor weakness and the prior futures relief remain the relevant historical context.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters now reports Brent $96.14 and WTI $84.88, versus previously reported $96.25 and $84.78. Differences are small and quote times are not established. Open Watch remains at 181 events; no material change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The latest oil reports do not indicate a decisive reversal of the supply premium. Overseas equity gains support a tactical bounce but cannot establish US semiconductor leadership. Prior Treasury and Fed pricing are lagged; cash equity impact remains prospective.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 27: shortened session may see a relief bounce that is vulnerable to fading. Monday November 30: normal liquidity and weekend OPEC+ policy may amplify or reduce the oil premium. Tuesday December 1: JOLTS and tentative semiconductor earnings could redirect the path.
editorial.bullCase: A sustained oil retreat, stronger semiconductor relative performance and wider Nasdaq participation could turn the holiday bounce into a durable recovery. Wednesday bargain buying provides some evidence of demand.
editorial.bearCase: Persistent supply risk and tariff uncertainty could reinforce inflation and financing concerns. Weak semiconductor leadership and a failed Friday bounce would increase Monday downside risk; no new isolated cash reaction is established.
editorial.watchNext: Verify timestamped Brent and WTI, Friday QQQ/SOX relative returns, VXN/VIX, Nasdaq advance-decline, paired 2Y/10Y yields and Fed pricing. Watch November 29 OPEC+ and December 1 JOLTS; confirm issuer earnings dates.
